Hermite double-node interpolation of exp(yt) has nonnegative remainder y^{2q}exp(y xi)/(2q)! product(t−x_i)², strictly positive in Gaussian integral for y≠0, so P_q(y)<y²/2 for all real nonzero y. Orthogonality yields degree-2q moment deficit q!, hence P_q=y²/2−(q!/(2q)!) y^{2q}+O(y^{2q+2}). Entropy-rate ≤ marginal Shannon entropy is an equality only for Bernoulli, and quadratic Legendre duality reduces all invariant measures exactly to F_beta(y)=P_q(y)−y²/(2 beta) for beta>0, with beta=0 treated by the base Bernoulli entropy maximum. Its coercive global strict-gap property proves beta≤1 unique base law, beta>1 positive symmetric maximizers and localization near zero as beta↓1; monotonic P_q′(y)/y near zero establishes exactly two locally, with the specified magnetization and pressure constants. A nonnegative squared vanishing polynomial excludes fewer than q support atoms; symmetry forces the q-atom nodal polynomial He_q and Vandermonde fixes weights. Independent Hermite quadrature numerical moments/deficit checked q=2..7, but the general proof is analytic.
